back: Complete (excess O₂): CO₂ + H₂O. Incomplete (limited O₂): CO and/or C + H₂O.
Binds to haemoglobin, stopping O₂ transport; colourless and odourless.

front: Least and most polluting fossil fuel?
back: Natural gas least CO₂ per kJ; coal most (plus SO₂, particulates).
Fuel from recently photosynthesised biomass — bioethanol, biodiesel, biogas.

Anode: H₂ → 2H⁺ + 2e⁻. Cathode: O₂ + 4H⁺ + 4e⁻ → 2H₂O.

front: Incomplete combustion of methane forming CO?
back: 2CH₄ + 3O₂ → 2CO + 4H₂O (or CH₄ + O₂ → C + 2H₂O forming soot).
C₂H₅OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O
Balance C (CO₂), then H (H₂O), then O last; use ½O₂ if needed, then double everything.
Respiratory problems, global dimming; deposit on surfaces. A sign of incomplete combustion (yellow, smoky flame).
Specific energy: energy released per unit mass (kJ kg⁻¹). Energy density: energy released per unit volume (kJ dm⁻³).
Coal, crude oil and natural gas — formed over millions of years from decayed organic matter under heat and pressure; non-renewable.

front: How do greenhouse gases warm the Earth?
back: Earth emits IR radiation; CO₂, CH₄ and H₂O absorb it (bond vibrations) and re-radiate some back towards the surface.
H₂O, CO₂, CH₄ (and N₂O); impact depends on abundance and ability to absorb IR.

front: How does increased CO₂ acidify oceans?
back: CO₂(aq) + H₂O(l) ⇌ H₂CO₃(aq) ⇌ H⁺(aq) + HCO₃⁻(aq) — pH falls, damaging coral and shells (CaCO₃).
Not in practice: CO₂ absorbed in photosynthesis equals that released on burning, but farming, fertilisers, processing and transport release extra CO₂.
Compete with food crops for land and water; deforestation; ethanol has lower specific energy than petrol and absorbs water.
6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ (light energy, chlorophyll).
A voltaic cell that converts chemical energy of a continuously supplied fuel and oxidant into electrical energy.
Anode: H₂ + 2OH⁻ → 2H₂O + 2e⁻. Cathode: O₂ + 2H₂O + 4e⁻ → 4OH⁻. Overall: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O.
Anode: CH₃OH + H₂O → CO₂ + 6H⁺ + 6e⁻. Cathode: O₂ + 4H⁺ + 4e⁻ → 2H₂O.

front: Advantages and disadvantages of fuel cells vs combustion?
back: Pro: more efficient, only H₂O from H₂, quiet. Con: expensive catalysts (Pt), H₂ storage and production often from fossil fuels.
